idiom_name: repository struct owning PgPool + impl FromRow for the domain type
implementation_notes: Rust has no reflection-based ORM in the standard library, so the mapper is a repository type that owns a connection pool and hand-written FromRow/From<Row> implementations (or the sqlx derive, which only matches column names to fields). The domain type stays a plain struct that never mentions a table, and query_as/fetch_one is the only place that knows SQL; the query! macro additionally type-checks the SQL against the database at compile time. Map explicit values rather than relying on positional order, and keep the mapper in its own crate/module so the domain crate never depends on sqlx.
pitfalls: Option<T> is mandatory for nullable columns: decoding NULL into String is a runtime error (UnexpectedNullError), so nullability must be part of the mapper's types.
Rows borrow from the connection, so mapped values must be owned before the query future ends - the mapper returns owned structs, never references into a row.
try_get is by name and fails at runtime for a renamed column; surface that as a mapper error rather than unwrapping it into a panic.
The sqlx macros need DATABASE_URL or SQLX_OFFLINE at build time; keep them in the mapper module so the compile-time check does not force the domain crate into a database dependency.

variants.name: Diesel schema module with Queryable/Selectable derives
variants.implementation_notes: Diesel generates the mapper from derives: table! declares the schema, #[derive(Queryable, Selectable, Insertable)] tells Diesel how to build the domain struct from a query's columns, and the query builder is typed against that schema, so a mismatched column type is a compile error. The struct therefore carries a compile-time link to the schema, and Diesel's connection/transaction API is the unit of work. Choose it when you want the database schema expressed once in Rust and checked by the compiler; keep the table! module in the persistence layer and the domain struct as plain data.
pitfalls: The derive maps by column order, not by name: selecting columns in a different order silently swaps fields whenever their types coincide - prefer Selectable with Customer::as_select().
Adding a field to the struct without updating table! and every select list breaks compilation in unrelated call sites; the schema module becomes a shared hot spot.
Diesel connections are not Sync, so mappers own a pool and check out a connection per operation; a long-lived connection shared across tasks is not possible by design.
